This is a concrete, verifiable scope/performance/architecture concern — an unconditioned network round-trip and DB write on every service construction for all deployments — but it is not clearly incorrect behavior (token refresh may succeed normally), so it is a substantive non-bug review concern rather than a confirmed defect.

judged_text: This PR adds an ungated Salesforce token refresh — a POST to login.salesforce.com plus a prisma.credential.update — that executes on every SalesforceCalendarService construction, is not routed through refreshOAuthTokens, and is not gated by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED unlike every other behavior change in the diff. Every Salesforce calendar operation on every deployment (including ones that will never use credential sharing) now pays an extra OAuth round-trip and a DB write per service construction, and the response.statusText !== 'OK' gate converts any proxy that strips the reason phrase or any Salesforce error body into a thrown HttpError that kills the operation — a scope expansion traceable to no stated requirement.
